commits.subject: fix: invite links without the slash scope, status back to online, beta code is enough
commits.body:
INVITE LINKS WERE THE MISSING PIECE

Discord only registers slash commands for servers the bot was invited
to with the `applications.commands` scope. Without it the bot joins,
prefix works, and the / menu stays empty no matter how often it syncs.

Two of the links the bot hands out were broken:

  * `/invite` pointed at client_id 1396114795102470196 -- a completely
    different bot. Anyone inviting through it got someone else's bot.
    Now uses self.bot.user.id, which cannot go stale.
  * The link in the mention menu had no scope parameter at all, so
    Discord assumed `bot` only.

While checking the command tree I also found the owner cog failing to
load entirely: `aiohttp` is used in its setup() and was never imported,
so the NameError took all 23 owner commands with it. One red line among
147 green ones in the log.

Added `!syncslash` for when Discord is being slow: global by default,
`!syncslash hier` for this server only (instant, good for testing). It
names the rate limit explicitly, because that is the one failure that
waiting does not fix. The existing `!sync` syncs databases and is
untouched.

What I checked and found *fine*: the tree holds 73 commands, no
duplicates, no name or description violates Discord's limits, and every
payload builds. The 146 hybrid commands are 72 top-level plus
subcommands -- nothing is missing.

STATUS BACK TO ONLINE

I misread the last request and pinned do_not_disturb. That was my
mistake. It is one constant, so this is a one-line change -- which is
why it was worth putting it in one place.

THE BETA CODE IS THE ONLY HURDLE

In the Speedrun tab, the beta code alone now unlocks every released
template, including clan. Premium is no longer a second gate there: the
code is handed out individually, and someone who has it should not hit
another wall.

In the template bot's !start menu clan stays premium -- that split is
unchanged. Only this path is open.

/start still verifies the template exists, so a typo fails immediately
instead of halfway through a build, and it refuses when the template
bot is unreachable.

Mutation test: 18/18 caught, tree byte-identical afterwards. Two of
those needed sharper tests first -- one of my own checks matched the
comment I had written above the link it was meant to verify.

Verified: 65 test files pass, 147 cogs boot, 541 prefix and 73 app
commands.
Not verified: nothing ran against real Discord -- no token, no browser.
Whether the / menu fills up shows only after a redeploy, and re-inviting
with the fixed link may be needed on servers added through the old one.

commits.subject: fix: no slash commands, status stuck online, premium bypass on /start
commits.body:
NO SLASH COMMANDS

Three things went wrong together, and the result was: prefix works,
the / menu is empty.

  1. The sync ran *after* run_sync(TOKEN). That emoji sync replaces the
     process with os.execv the moment it patches emoji.py -- everything
     after it is never reached. The sync now runs first.

  2. on_ready fires on every reconnect, not just at startup. Discord
     allows only a handful of global command syncs per day, so a bot
     that loses its connection a few times hits the rate limit and then
     syncs nothing at all. A module-level flag now allows it once per
     process, and clears itself on failure so the next reconnect can
     retry.

  3. A failed sync was printed and vanished among a thousand lines of
     startup output. It goes to logging.exception now, with traceback.
     An empty tree is logged as a warning too -- it syncs fine and
     delivers nothing.

STATUS STUCK ON ONLINE

The constructor set do_not_disturb; the presence loop then called
change_presence(activity=...) with no status. discord.py turns that
into Status.online -- literally "if status is None: status =
Status.online" in Client.change_presence. So the first tick after
startup overwrote the setting, permanently.

The status is now passed on every call and lives in one constant
(PRESENCE_STATUS) instead of two places that drifted apart.

PREMIUM BYPASS

Adding the Clan Server surfaced this: /speedrun/templates marks premium
templates as locked and the dashboard greys them out, but
/speedrun/start only ever checked the beta list. Calling the endpoint
directly built any premium template without premium -- the same shape
of hole the beta gate had before.

/start now asks the template bot which templates are premium and
refuses when the caller has none. It denies on failure rather than
allowing: an unreachable template bot must not hand out paid templates,
and the build would fail without it anyway. No second list of premium
keys here -- that would drift.

Clan is in BETA_TEMPLATES, so the Speedrun tab offers five templates.
The !start menu in the template bot already handled it correctly:
it reads registry.free / registry.premium, and clan.premium is true.

Mutation test: 14/14 caught, tree byte-identical afterwards.
Verified: 65 test files pass, 147 cogs boot, 73 app commands in the tree.
Not verified: nothing ran against real Discord -- no token, no browser.
In particular I could not watch a real sync happen or see the status
in a client.

commits.subject: feat: emoji picker on every text field, Clan Server in the beta list
commits.body:
THE EMOJI PICKER WAS NEVER RESTRICTED

You asked for the emojis to work on every server. Checking first: they
already did. The picker sits in the "Eigene Nachricht" tab, which
exists on every server, and neither the route nor the proxy ever
limited it to the support server -- only the ready-made changelog
templates are gated that way. The emojis themselves are application
emojis, which Discord renders anywhere the bot can post.

What was actually missing: the picker only sat on two of the fields.
The embed branch had none at all, and neither did the button emoji
input -- exactly where a custom emoji is most obvious. Added to title,
description, author, footer and buttons.

Each embed field has its own limit (title 256, description 4096,
footer 2048), so the guard takes the limit as an argument instead of
hardcoding 2000. Discord counts them separately, and a truncated emoji
code leaves a bare number in the text.

CLAN SERVER

Built like the Gaming Hub, but everything revolves around the clan
rather than individual games: clan-talk instead of a squad lobby,
fight-call before the match, war-room for planning. Plus war planning,
training rooms and an application forum.

85 channels, 25 of them voice, 20 roles from recruit to clan leader.
Added to BETA_TEMPLATES so it is selectable in the Speedrun tab.

Two closed areas: "premium" (VIP, boosters, partners, staff) and
"mitglieder" (the roster). Both use the existing visibility tiers.

TESTS

The new picker checks caught two of my own weak assertions:
  * one searched for the first `text.length` guard and reported the
    new embed one as a failure -- there are two now, and they look
    different on purpose;
  * one sliced the embed branch at the first `kind === "embed"`, which
    is the type selector at the top, giving a thirty-character
    fragment that proved nothing.

commits.subject: feat(compose): pick the bot's own emojis, plus four new changelog entries
commits.body:
THE EMOJI PICKER

The bot ships around 140 custom emojis. Using one in a message meant
knowing its exact spelling -- `<:name:1530375445785084005>`, eighteen
digit id included. In practice: copy it out of the source, or type
`\:name:` in a chat and paste the result back.

There is now a picker next to every text field in the compose tab.
Tiles, grouped by purpose, searchable. A click inserts the emoji at the
cursor, not at the end -- needing one mid-sentence and then dragging it
into place is the kind of small annoyance that makes a feature unused.

The list is read from utils/emoji.py through the syntax tree, not
maintained a second time here. A hand-kept copy drifts apart the first
time an emoji is added, and nobody notices until raw text shows up in a
message. Reading it by AST also skips the dictionaries, helpers and
aliases in that module, which a dir() would have swept up.

Grouping started with more than half of them in "Sonstige", which is
not wrong but useless as a way to find anything. Added rules for
navigation, devices, badges and fun; that is down to 13 genuine
oddments now.

Two details that matter in use: duplicate codes are dropped (DELETE and
DELETE_ALT1 are the same emoji, two identical tiles only confuse), and
animated ones preview as GIF rather than a still frame.

FOUR NEW CHANGELOG ENTRIES

Everything since the last one on 01.08, on the support server only:

  04.08  Speedrun templates -- three new ones, switches now match
  03.08  Speedrun access -- beta code per server, admin management
  02.08  Speedrun runs without the tab -- the worst bug of the batch
  02.08  Ticket permissions -- anyone could close somebody else's

They use real emoji codes, and a test checks that against the source:
an invented id renders as raw text, which is exactly the failure the
30.07 changelog was about. Codes inside backticks are excluded -- that
older entry deliberately shows a broken one as an example.

Not built: the variables (member count, server name) discussed earlier.
You said to leave them out.

commits.subject: fix(speedrun): the sidebar style never applied, and steps ignored the template
commits.body:
THE SIDEBAR ROW

You reported it and you were right: the row looked like every other one
in the real dashboard, while the preview showed it styled.

The sidebar has two rendering paths -- one for top-level entries
(Premium, Admin) and one for items inside a group. "Speedrun (Beta)"
sits in the "Verwaltung" group, so it renders through the second. All
the styling was written in the first. Premium looked right precisely
because Premium is a top-level entry.

The group branch now knows the row too: cyan frame, lit left edge,
domed icon tile, BETA tag.

The existing test did not catch this. It checked that "isSpeedrun"
appeared *somewhere* in the file -- which it did, in the branch that
never runs. It now checks the branch that actually renders the row,
and that the row is recognised by its href rather than a constant.

STEPS NOW FOLLOW THE CHOSEN TEMPLATE

/speedrun/steps returned the same thirteen steps regardless of what the
template builds, all switched on. Twelve of thirteen templates had
switches set to "on" for things that never appear: "minimal" has no
verify gate, no tickets, no self-roles; "rp" has no roles channel;
only "community" has a counting channel. Leaving them on produced
"skipped" in the report afterwards -- the user had enabled something
that could never work, and only found out at the end.

The template bot now reports its capabilities per step, /speedrun/steps
passes them through, and the tab greys out what cannot happen and says
why. If the template bot is unreachable, all steps stay offered: an
overly generous list is better than an empty one.

THREE NEW TEMPLATES

music, dev and minimal are added to the beta list. They are the reason
the step problem became visible -- "minimal" deliberately has none of
verify, tickets or self-roles.

tests/test_speedrun_templates.py checks the step list against the real
registry of the template repo, and skips cleanly when that repo is not
checked out next to this one.

commits.subject: feat(speedrun): gate the tab behind a beta code, with admin management
commits.body:
Three things: a code gate on the tab, an admin panel to manage it, and
a sidebar row that looks like what it opens.

THE GATE

The tab is closed until somebody types the beta code. What gets
unlocked is a *server*, not an account -- the Speedrun rebuilds one
specific server, and an unlock tied to a user would follow them onto
every server they have rights on.

The check lives in the bot, not the browser. An overlay is a door
without a wall: /start is an HTTP route, and curl does not ask for an
overlay. Every acting endpoint calls _require_unlocked() first.

The code is accepted case-insensitively and with collapsed whitespace,
and both spellings work -- the one that was handed out has "Univertiy"
in it. Rejecting that would lock out exactly the people the beta is
for, and the screen would only say "wrong code". It is stored hashed:
the same table records who did what and when, and a secret has no
business in a log.

REVOKE VS BAN

Two different things, deliberately.

  Revoke  The code has to be entered again. For a server changing
          hands, or a code that got passed around.
  Ban     No code helps any more.

Both abort a running Speedrun immediately. Taking someone's access
while the bot keeps rebuilding their server for another ten minutes
would be the wrong half of a decision.

A ban outranks the code -- checked before the code, or a banned server
frees itself with the right input. Revoking a banned server keeps the
ban. Lifting a ban does *not* restore access: an unbanned server types
the code again, because a lifted ban is not an unlock.

THE ADMIN PANEL

New tab under Admin > Verwaltung: every server that entered the code,
who unlocked it and when, how many runs it has done, and the full
history including failed attempts -- forty rejected guesses is a
different thing from one typo. Guild names and member counts come from
the bot cache; a list of eighteen-digit IDs is unusable for this.

Reachable only for global admins, enforced in the proxy. That rule sits
*before* the guild-id check: "admin" is not an eighteen-digit number and
would otherwise be rejected as a missing guild_id.

THE SIDEBAR ROW

A lit edge on the left, a domed icon tile, and the "(Beta)" in the
label replaced by a small tag. The travelling light stays the only
moving part -- two animations next to each other compete.

TESTS

tests/test_speedrun_access.py, twenty groups against a real SQLite file.
Mutation test: 17/17 caught, tree byte-identical afterwards.

Also fixed two flaky tests of my own from the previous commit: they
slept 2.3s waiting on a 2.0s task, which failed under the load of the
full suite while nothing was wrong with the code. They wait on events
now -- stable across eight parallel runs.

Verified: 62 test files pass, 147 cogs boot, next build clean.
Not verified: nothing ran against real Discord -- no token, no browser.

commits.subject: fix(speedrun): the setup hung on an open browser tab, and cancel lied
commits.body:
Four faults, each reproduced before it was fixed.

1. The handover depended on the browser staying open.

   Only the dashboard started the second half: it polled progress, saw
   "build done" and called /finish. Close the tab during the build --
   phone locks, network drops, window closed -- and nobody ever made
   that call. Roles and channels stood, but verify, tickets, logging,
   anti-nuke, levels and the welcome message were missing, with no
   message at all. A build takes over a minute; keeping a tab open that
   long is not a condition you can put on people.

   The bot now waits for the build itself (_watch_build) and hands over
   on its own. The panel only watches.

2. Cancelling did not cancel.

   The route set the state to "failed" and nothing else. The setup kept
   running and wrote "done" over it seconds later -- the tab jumped from
   "cancelled" back to "finished" while half the server was missing.
   The run is now marked, the tasks are really cancelled, and the
   finally branch respects the mark.

3. A hiccup at the template bot blanked the main bot's progress.

   /status raised 502 whenever the template bot was unreachable, even
   though the main bot's state lives in memory here and the template
   bot is not needed during setup at all. A redeploy over there made
   the tab go blank mid-setup. Its absence is now reported as a note.

4. The template list undercounted roles.

   It counted only the accent roles from the JSON file: "3 roles" on a
   template that creates 16, because the base ladder is added by the
   builder. Channel counts and a per-category outline now ship too, so
   the choice shows what actually gets built.

Also in the tab: one progress bar across both halves (it used to sit at
100% for the whole setup), elapsed time, a searchable log with a
"problems only" filter, failures listed before successes, and three
follow-up steps after a run.

tests/test_speedrun_watchdog.py covers all of it against real flows.
Mutation test: 15/15 caught, tree byte-identical afterwards.

Verified: 61 test files pass, 147 cogs boot, next build clean.
Not verified: nothing ran against real Discord -- no token, no browser.

commits.subject: fix(tickets): anyone could close somebody else's ticket
commits.body:
The ticket buttons -- Claim, Lock, Close -- were guarded by a staff-role
check on `TicketActionsView`. The check never ran.

`from_embed(embed, view)` moves the buttons out of the given view and
into a new Panel, because a component belongs to exactly one view. The
original view keeps its `interaction_check` and is never sent. Discord
calls the check of the view a message was *sent* with -- so the guard sat
on an object nobody would ever interact with.

Reproduced: build a view with a check that always denies, run it through
`from_embed`, and the resulting panel has no check at all. Three call
sites affected, all in ticket.py, found by walking the AST for
`from_embed(_, X)` where X defines `interaction_check`.

Fixed in `from_embed` rather than at the three call sites: the next view
with a check would hit exactly the same trap. The check is carried on
the *instance*, bound to the original view -- it reads `self.cog` and
`self.cat_id`, so re-binding it to the panel would only produce
AttributeError the moment somebody clicks. On the class it would leak
one ticket's check into every panel built afterwards.

Also in this commit, the logging tab rebuilt. Nine identical cards were
the wrong answer to the question people actually have, which is not
"which of nine event types do I want" but "I want to see what happens on
my server". Now three levels: a one-click preset, three groups, or the
individual types folded away. The noisy one (reactions, one line per
emoji click) is only in "everything", and it says so before you choose
rather than in a footnote afterwards.

While doing that: the panel read `channel_info.cannot_post`, which the
server never sent. A channel the bot cannot write in looked exactly like
a working one -- switch on, channel picked, all green, nothing ever
arrives. That is the most common cause behind "logging is broken". The
API reports it now.

Two of my own mistakes here, both worth naming:

  * I overwrote tests/test_logging_tab.py -- 695 lines, four checks
    about which event reaches which category. Restored from git; mine
    live in test_logging_ui.py, which is the honest split anyway: one
    file for the module, one for the tab.
  * I guessed the save bar's props (`dirty`, `onReset`) instead of
    reading them. TypeScript caught it. A test pins the real ones now.

Checked: 19 new checks across two files, mutation test 12/12. Boot test
147 cogs. Full suite green, 60 files. Build clean, and the two
exhaustive-deps warnings I introduced are gone -- `x || []` makes a new
array every render, so the useMemo around it never held.

Not tested: clicking an actual ticket button on a real server.

commits.subject: fix(tickets): opening one produced an empty channel, and the panel lied
commits.body:
Three faults, all reproduced before touching anything.

**The dashboard said dropdown, Discord showed buttons.** The speedrun
built the view out of buttons unconditionally while the database said
"dropdown". Worse than just inconsistent: the ticket cog rebuilds the
view from `panel_type` after a restart, so the message would have looked
different after the next deploy than it did the day before.

**Opening a ticket produced an empty channel.** Two faults in one line,
either of which is enough on its own:

  * `set_image(TICKET_CHANNEL_IMAGE_URL)` pointed at a Discord
    attachment URL with an expiry signature. Checked: it returns 403.
    Discord rejects the whole message over the dead image.
  * `content=` alongside a Components V2 view. With the V2 flag there is
    no content field at all -- Discord's own docs say content and embeds
    stop working once the flag is set. Answer is 50035.

The mentions do need a content field, or nobody gets pinged. So two
messages now: the pings as plain text, then the card. And the greeting
is German, like the rest of what the bot says.

The dead URL is gone entirely rather than left unused, with a note
saying why an attachments link is unusable for a permanent message.

**Level XP had no consequences.** The system was switched on and no role
was ever handed out. Three rewards now (level 5/15/30), and a role above
the bot is skipped with a reason rather than written to a table where it
would silently do nothing.

Also added: invite tracking as its own step, and the sidebar row got its
own look. Premium is amber and pulses, Admin is indigo with a tile --
this one takes cyan plus a light that travels along the top edge every
4.5 seconds. Slow on purpose: it sits in a sidebar somebody looks at all
day. Off entirely under prefers-reduced-motion, because a frozen bright
line reads as a rendering fault.

Two of my own test mistakes, both caught by the mutation run:

  * The "no content with a V2 view" check used the regex
    `send\(\s*content=[^)]*view=from_embed`. `[^)]*` stops at the first
    bracket -- which is inside `" ".join(pings)`. The offending call sat
    right there and went unseen. Now over the AST.
  * The sidebar test looked for `@keyframes speedrun-sweep`. Renaming
    the keyframe left the rule in place, the animation pointing at
    nothing, and the test green. It now checks the animation is
    referenced and that the name resolves.

Checked: 17 new checks. Mutation test 10/10. Boot test 147 cogs. Full
suite green, 58 files. Verified the sweep survives into the built CSS,
not just the source.

Not tested: opening an actual ticket against Discord, and no browser
here -- the sidebar row was checked in a standalone preview.

commits.subject: refactor(dashboard): rebuild the Speedrun tab, fix six faults in it
commits.body:
Rewritten from scratch. Every fault below was reproduced first, then
fixed, and each has a test that fails when it comes back.

**1. Duplicate log lines.** `setInterval` fired the next request whether
or not the previous one had finished. When a response took longer than
the tick, the second read the same counter as the first and fetched the
same lines again. Reproduced with a 2.5s response on a 1.5s tick: 10
lines instead of 5, every one doubled. Now a loop that waits for the
result before scheduling again, plus a latch against overlap.

**2. Reloading lost the build.** The load path never asked for the
status, so after F5 you were back on step 1 while the build carried on
invisibly -- and the start button would have kicked off a second one. It
now checks for a running job, replays the lines so the output does not
start mid-sentence, and jumps to the terminal.

**3. The handover could trigger itself.** The condition was "template
done and handover not run yet", which a fifteen-minute-old job also
satisfies. Every run now carries a `run_id`; the bot rejects one that
belongs to a different run. Checked server-side, not just here.

**4. The timer restarted on every toggle**, because the poll callback
depended on `options`. The options travel through a ref now.

**5. "Partially done" looked like "done".** The state existed in the
backend and the display did not know it, so a run with gaps was
indistinguishable from a clean one -- you would scroll past the red
lines. It has its own phase, its own icon and a sentence saying what to
look at.

**6. No way out.** A stuck build left the tab on "running" forever with
a second attempt blocked. There is a cancel button, and it says plainly
that the server stays half-built, because it does.

Motion added deliberately quietly: rows stagger in, the progress bar has
a sheen while it moves, the terminal has a blinking caret, the running
step pulses. All of it switches off under prefers-reduced-motion -- for
some people that is not taste, it is nausea.

Three of my own test mistakes, all caught by the mutation run:

  * The hook-order test searched for the first `    return (` and
    compared what came after. That matched a nested JSX return deep in
    the output, so the comparison point sat behind every hook and the
    test could not find anything. Then I over-corrected to `{6,}` spaces
    and missed the loading branch, which has four.
  * The overlap latch was checked with `"pollingRef.current" in tick` --
    still true after removing the guard, because releasing it in the
    finally block contains the same string.
  * Filtering hook matches by indentation let through exactly the case
    the test exists for: a `useState` right after the early return.

Checked: 25 new checks, mutation test 11/11. Full suite green, 58 files.
Build clean, tsc clean.

Not tested: an actual run against Discord, and no browser here -- the
animations were verified in a standalone preview, not in the app.

commits.subject: fix(tickets): opening a ticket failed, and the overview never saw them
commits.body:
Four faults reported, all four traced to a cause before touching
anything.

**Opening a ticket did nothing.** The ticket cog reads
`discord_category_id` to know where to put the new channel, and my
speedrun step never set it. Every click answered "This ticket category
has been deleted or is misconfigured". The panel looked finished and was
inert. It now passes the Discord category the ticket channel itself sits
under.

**Tickets were missing from the overview.** That page reads
`guild_configs`; the speedrun only wrote `ticket_panels`. So "Tickets"
showed as not configured while the panel hung in the channel.

While checking that, two more modules turned out to have been reported
wrong on *every* server since forever: the overview only knows how to
read SQLite, but logging keeps its config in
`jsondb/logging_config.json` and counting in `db/counting.json`. Both
were permanently "not set up". Added a JSON path for them, and the list
is sorted by name now so storage format does not decide the order.

**Dropdown instead of buttons**, for tickets and for the role picker.
The role picker used reactions, and reactions are the worse tool here: a
reaction is one emoji, so two roles with the same emoji cannot be told
apart, and a reaction removed by hand desyncs silently. The picker is
now a persistent Select handled by a new cog, with duplicate emojis
dropped -- the whole point of moving away from reactions was that you
cannot distinguish two identical ones.

**The welcome message.** German, with the server name and icon as the
author line, member number in the text, "by University Bot" as the
footer. Two traps avoided by reading the code rather than guessing:

  * The placeholders are `{server_name}` and `{server_membercount}`.
    `{server}` would have been left standing in the text verbatim.
  * build_embed() reads flat keys `author_name` / `footer_text`. A
    nested `{"author": {...}}` is ignored without complaint -- the line
    would simply have been absent.

Also: the log channels are now on the ignore list. Without that each log
entry logs the next one -- the bot writes to #nachrichten-logs, that is
a new message, so it writes again.

Checked: 20 new checks. Mutation test 11/11, including all four reported
faults. One of those started green: my fixtures happened to use
different emojis, so the de-duplication never ran. Added a case with two
identical ones.

Boot test: 147 cogs, 540 prefix, 73 app commands. Full suite green.

Not tested: opening an actual ticket on a real server. No token here.

commits.subject: fix(welcome): the banner never showed, and two channels stayed empty
commits.body:
Three faults, all of them mine from last round.

**The welcome banner did not appear.** The renderer worked; the sending
did not. The image went along as a file *next to* the message, but a
Components V2 message renders only its components -- Discord uploaded
the attachment and never displayed it. So the old greeting kept coming
through without a picture.

Reproduced before touching anything: rendered the greeting panel and
counted component types. No media component, exactly as the user saw it.

Fixed with Panel.add_image(), which puts a MediaGallery *inside* the
container. Next to it would sit outside the card -- the same mistake the
J2C buttons made. Plain-text greetings get their own panel, otherwise
the banner had nowhere to go there either.

**The role picker channel stayed empty.** I took the dropdown away from
the template bot last round, on the grounds that the main bot owns the
roles, and then did not build the replacement. Now there is a step:
panel plus reactions, one per role. Roles above the bot are left out
rather than listed -- a button that does nothing when clicked is worse
than an absent one.

**The rules channel stayed empty**, same cause. Six short rules that fit
any server, and the panel says outright they are a template to adapt. A
wall of twenty points is not read, and what is not read cannot be
enforced.

Also: tickets use buttons instead of a dropdown (with a single category
a menu is one click too many, and you cannot even see what is in it
before opening), and the new panels carry the app's own emojis.

Three of my tests were weak and the mutation run caught them:

  * The long-name test called _fit() itself and checked its result. The
    mutation did not break _fit -- it made render() stop using it. The

commits.subject: feat(speedrun): welcome banner with avatar, plus counting, leveling and J2C
commits.body:
Four things asked for, all in the handover the main bot runs after the
template bot has built the server.

**Welcome banner.** An image with the member's avatar: dark navy like
the dashboard, a round avatar with a glowing ring in the bot's colour,
the name large, server and member number underneath. Two blurred halos
rather than one -- a single layer looks either muddy or flat.

Everything about it can fail without taking the greeting down: Pillow
missing, avatar download timing out, a corrupt image. Each stage catches
for itself and the greeting goes out without the picture. A welcome that
crashes is worse than a plain one; the member is in the server either
way.

The name shrinks to fit instead of being cut off with an ellipsis -- a
long username is exactly the case where somebody wants to see their own
name. And the member number is spelled out with a thousands separator,
not "1.2K": on a joining number the exact figure is the whole point.

Rendering runs in a thread. Pillow takes a few hundred milliseconds and
would otherwise block the event loop, which stalls the entire bot during
a join wave.

**Counting now actually runs.** The template bot creates the channel and
writes a 1 into it, but in the main bot the game sat at enabled=False
with channel=None. The channel looked finished and answered no number --
exactly as reported. The step switches it on and starts at 1, because
the 1 is already posted; starting at 0 would make the bot expect a 1
next and reject the 2.

**Leveling and Join to Create** as steps of their own, and **automod is
now on by default**. That last one is a reversal: I had it off, arguing
it acts on every message. Wrong trade-off. A fresh server without a spam
brake is what advertising bots look for, and whoever runs a speedrun
wants a finished server -- not one with a protection quietly disabled.
Staff roles are exempt and five messages in ten seconds is not something
anyone types by accident.

**The ticket panel is posted, not just prepared.** It used to be created
and left for the user to find the "Tickets" tab and press send. A
speedrun that stops halfway is not one. Same view the API route builds,
called from one place, so the two cannot drift apart.

Two of my own mistakes fixed along the way:

  * The test helper cleared db_manager._connections without closing
    them. Every aiosqlite connection holds a thread, so the test file
    finished its work and then hung forever on exit -- it went from a
    300s timeout to 0.8s.
  * Every step must be individually switchable, which nothing checked.
    Now asserted for all ten.

Checked: 12 new checks against real SQLite files, read back the way the
cogs read them. Banner rendered for real and looked at, including the
long-name case. Boot test green: 146 cogs, 540 prefix, 73 app commands.
Full suite green, 57 files, build clean.

Not tested: an actual join against Discord. No token here, so the banner
has never gone through Discord's own image pipeline.

commits.body:
Asked for: an option under "Advanced" that deletes every channel and
role before building. The builder in the template bot could already do
it (BuildMode.REBUILD, tested there), but the dashboard sent
`rebuild: false` hard-coded, so there was no way to reach it.

This is the only switch in the whole tab that destroys instead of adds,
and Discord has no recycle bin. So it is off by default -- a deletion
you merely fail to untick is a trap -- and it needs the server name
typed out before the button unlocks.

The confirmation is checked in the BOT, not just in the browser.
Anyone calling the endpoint with curl skips every dialog the dashboard
puts up, and `options.rebuild=true` is quick to type. The permissions
are checked up front too: what the bot cannot delete stays, and then the
server sits there half emptied with no explanation.

Two of my own tests were worthless and the mutation run caught them:

  * The wipe guard was checked by searching for text. Replacing
    `if confirm != guild.name` with `if False` left every one of those
    strings in place, so the test stayed green with the guard gone.
    Rewritten over the AST: the branch must not be constant, must
    compare the name, and must raise -- all on the same `if`.
  * `options = {}` (silently dropping everything the user picked) also
    passed. Now it is asserted that options come from `data` and are
    passed on.
  * Same shape in the UI test: `setWipeConfirm("")` merely being present
    proved nothing, since it survives behind `if (false)`. Now the
    handler body is read.

green, 57 files, build clean.

Note on the .env the user posted: TEMPLATE_BOT_URL points at the public
https address, and that one works -- reachable from here, /health
answers, the speedrun route responds. The internal address would be
better (no detour over the internet, no public exposure) but it is not

commits.subject: fix(dashboard): stop one failed call from blanking the whole Speedrun tab
commits.body:
The requirements step showed every check as missing even though both
bots were there. That was my bug, and it was the wrong half of the
screen: the failure was on the template bot, the display blamed the main
one.

The tab loads three things at once -- the precheck, the templates and
the step list. They ran through `Promise.all`, which rejects as soon as
ONE of them fails and throws away the results of the others. The
template bot was unreachable, `/templates` returned 502, and with it the
successful precheck response went in the bin. `pre` stayed null, so
every requirement rendered as a red cross.

Now `Promise.allSettled` with each result handled on its own, plus two
separate error slots. A broken template list says nothing about whether
the bots are present, and the tab must not pretend otherwise. Both
errors are shown where they belong instead of silently becoming
"missing".

Also: "Template bot unreachable" was a useless message. It covered three
completely different causes needing three different fixes. The 502 now
names the one that applies:

  * connection refused -> the service is down, or it only listens on
    IPv4 while Railway's private network is IPv6-only
  * unknown host       -> TEMPLATE_BOT_URL is wrong or missing, likely
                          without the port (plain http tries 80)
  * timeout            -> how many seconds it waited

Checked: 16 new checks. Mutation-tested 16/16, including the four that
reproduce exactly what went wrong here -- `Promise.all`, an ignored
precheck result, and either error being swallowed. The 502 test asserts
the two causes get DIFFERENT messages, since a single shared wording is
how this cost a debugging round in the first place.

The other half of this bug is in the template bot repo: it bound to
0.0.0.0 and was therefore invisible on Railway's IPv6-only private
network.

commits.subject: feat(dashboard): finish the Speedrun tab and hand the server to the main bot
commits.body:
Stage two of the Speedrun. Stage one could already make the template bot
build a server; what was missing was the tab itself and everything that
happens after the build.

The tab, four steps in the order they depend on each other:

  1. Requirements  both bots present, both allowed to manage the server
  2. Template      only `community` in the beta, premium included
  3. Scope         "standard: everything", expandable to single switches
  4. Run           a terminal, line by line, colour-coded per bot

After the template bot finishes, the University Bot takes over and sets
up verification, the log channels, anti-nuke, tickets, the welcome
message and the auto role. Automod is off by default: it acts on every
message, and on a fresh server somebody should decide that themselves.

The hard part was not the wiring, it was knowing WHICH channel is the
verify channel. Channel names are small caps with an emoji prefix
(`✅・ᴠᴇʀɪꜰɪᴢɪᴇʀᴇɴ`), so `"verify" in channel.name` finds nothing, and
guessing is worse than not acting: a gate in the wrong channel is only
noticed when the first people cannot get in. So core/handover.py builds
the map on the template bot's side, where the definition is still
around: `widget == VERIFY` says which channel it is, `mode == LOG` which
one is a log channel, and the role keys were stable all along.

Every step runs on its own and fails on its own. A missing permission on
tickets must not take verification and the logs down with it, and the
terminal should show one red line, not a wall of them.

Two guards that took a second look:

  * The finish route fetches the map from the template bot rather than
    accepting it from the browser. Otherwise anyone with curl could send
    channel ids and have the bot post the verify panel wherever.
  * The poll starts the second half exactly once. Without the latch,
    every 1.5s tick would kick off another run.

Checked: 21 new checks over real SQLite files, read back the way the
cogs read them -- not through a mock. Mutation-tested at three levels:
9/9 on the handover map, 10/10 on the main bot steps, 12/12 on the tab.
Three of those started green and were real holes in my own tests; the
worst compared the log mapping against itself, so swapping two
categories went unnoticed.

Also fixed along the way:

  * A test of mine asserted `x is not None or x is None` -- a tautology
    that checks nothing. Replaced with a real check plus two for the
    cases it was supposed to cover.
  * test_navigation pinned "only anonchat is marked beta", so every new
    beta tab broke it for the wrong reason. It now checks what actually
    matters: tab bar and sidebar must agree.

Not tested: an actual build against Discord. No token and no server
here, and no browser to click through the tab.

commits.subject: feat(api): Speedrun-Weg zum Template-Bot
commits.body:
Vier Routen unter /api/v1/speedrun, die das Dashboard fuer den neuen
Beta-Reiter braucht:

  GET  /templates            waehlbare Templates, mit Sperrgrund
  GET  /{guild}/precheck     sind beide Bots da und duerfen sie?
  POST /{guild}/start        Bau starten
  GET  /{guild}/status       Fortschritt fuers Terminal

Das Dashboard redet nur mit diesem Bot, nie direkt mit dem
Template-Bot. Der Partner-Token darf den Browser nie erreichen -- ein
Dashboard, das drueben selbst anklopft, muesste ihn mitschicken oder
eine zweite Proxy-Schicht bauen. Diese Route ist die zweite Schicht,
und ein Test haelt fest, dass kein Endpunkt den Token zurueckgibt.

Keine neuen Variablen: TEMPLATE_BOT_URL und PREMIUM_PARTNER_TOKEN sind
vom Premium-Widerruf her schon eingerichtet. Fehlt eine, kommt 503 mit
dem Namen der fehlenden Variable statt eines 500ers -- man soll aus der
Fehlermeldung ablesen koennen, was zu tun ist.

Beta: nur `community` ist freigegeben, auch fuer Premium. Die anderen
neun Templates sind gebaut, aber noch nicht durch einen echten Server
gelaufen, und ein halb geprueftes Template auf einen fremden Server
anzuwenden laesst sich nicht rueckgaengig machen. Die Sperre sitzt im
Start-Endpunkt selbst, nicht nur in der Liste: sonst koennte jeder mit
curl daran vorbei.

precheck prueft einzeln -- University Bot da, Rechte da, Template-Bot
da -- damit das Dashboard sagen kann was fehlt. "Irgendetwas stimmt
nicht" ist die nutzloseste aller Fehlermeldungen. Ist die Client-ID
gesetzt, kommt gleich der Einladungslink mit.

Eine kaputte Premium-Abfrage gilt als "kein Premium": im Zweifel darf
niemand etwas bekommen, das er nicht bezahlt hat. Ein toter
Template-Bot wird zu 502 mit lesbarem Text statt zu einem Traceback.

Geprueft: 54 Testdateien gruen, 146 Cogs laden. Die neuen Tests decken
die Registrierung (404 hiesse: nicht eingehaengt), die 503-Meldung, die
Beta-Sperre im Start selbst, das Fail-Closed bei Premium, den 502-Fall
und dass der Token die Antwort nie verlaesst.

Eine Testpruefung war zuerst falsch -- sie teilte den Quelltext an
"return " und traf damit eine Hilfsfunktion statt eines Endpunkts. Sie
liest jetzt den AST.

Noch offen: der Reiter im Dashboard und die Uebergabe an den University
Bot (Verify, Anti-Nuke, Tickets). Der Bau sammelt dafuer schon alle

commits.subject: feat(dashboard): add a WARTUNG switch that takes the site offline
commits.body:
WARTUNG=true puts a notice in front of every path -- landing page,
dashboard, guild pages, anything that does not exist. Unset or false and
nothing changes at all.

The notice says what was asked for: maintenance, back around midnight,
closing a security hole, Fufi is on it -- and, in its own box, that the
Discord bot keeps working. That last part is the point of the page; a
site that is simply down makes people assume the bot is down too.

Two decisions worth spelling out
--------------------------------
The notice answers 200, not 503. start.sh waits for `curl /` to succeed
before it starts the bot and aborts the container on failure -- a 503
here would take down the very bot the page promises is still running.

It rewrites rather than redirects, so the address bar keeps the path the
visitor asked for and a refresh lands them where they wanted once
maintenance ends.

WARTUNG, not NEXT_PUBLIC_WARTUNG: a NEXT_PUBLIC_* value is baked into
the bundle when the image is built, so flipping the Railway variable
afterwards would change nothing.

The maintenance check runs before the auth check. withAuth sends
anonymous visitors to Discord to sign in, so the other order would
bounce people into an OAuth flow during an outage instead of telling
them what is going on.

The bypass
----------
/526etrzeqwgoqfu32qzi asks for a password -- default fufi67, override
with WARTUNG_PASSWORT -- and sets a cookie that lets that browser
through for eight hours. The comparison is a server action, so the
password never reaches the browser bundle, and the cookie holds a value
derived from it rather than the password itself.

Verified against a running server, not a mock: repro/wartung_live.py
boots the real standalone build twice, with and without the variable,
and checks six paths, the API's JSON 503, the bypass page, and that the
right cookie gets through while a wrong one does not. All green.

tests/test_wartung.py is the cheap version for the suite, and all 13
mutations fail it when reintroduced -- including the 503 that would kill
the container and the bypass path being locked out.

Not seen in a real browser: there is none here. The HTML was fetched
from the running server and read, but not rendered.

commits.subject: fix(panels): stop from_view wrapping a panel inside a panel
commits.body:
>help crashed:

    400 Bad Request (error code: 50035): Invalid Form Body
    In components.0.components.1.components.0:
    Value of field "type" must be one of (2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8).

Discord saying: something that is not a component turned up where one
belongs. It was a Container, stuffed into an ActionRow by from_view().

I caused this in the previous commit. The rewrite script decided what
was a plain View by class name, resolved locally -- and `View` in
utils/help.py is a LayoutView subclass. So from_view() was handed a
finished panel, took its Containers for components, and packed them
into an ActionRow.

Nineteen call sites matched that pattern; four are genuinely LayoutViews
(help, the trivia card, the logging setup panel, the server icon), and
every one of them would have thrown the moment the command ran. The
other fifteen were false positives in my own scan.

from_view() now hands a LayoutView straight back. That fixes all four at
once and makes the function safe to call on anything.

Why nothing caught it
---------------------
The suite was green, the bot booted, 146 cogs loaded, 53 files passed.
None of that looks at the shape of the tree that gets sent -- which is
the only place this bug exists.

tests/test_v2_nesting.py builds the trees and walks them: nothing but
buttons and selects inside an ActionRow, no Container inside a
Container, no row over five, no select sharing a row. It is run against
from_view, from_embed, the J2C panel and the real classes behind each
call site, resolved as objects rather than by name -- because guessing
from the name is exactly what went wrong.

Verified: 53 test files pass, 146 cogs load, and all 4 mutations fail
the suite when reintroduced -- including deleting the guard, which is
the bug as shipped.

Not tested against real Discord: no token here. The tree is now checked
against the rules Discord enforces, which is the closest this
environment gets.

commits.subject: fix(bot): put the J2C buttons inside the card, and finish the custom emoji
commits.body:
You were right -- there were still buttons outside the card, and the
Join-to-Create panel was the clearest example.

The bug every scan missed
-------------------------
ControlPanelView *is* a LayoutView. Every check I wrote called it
converted, because they all asked "is this a LayoutView?" and stopped
there. But its twelve buttons were added with self.add_item(ActionRow(...))
next to the container rather than into it:

    container = build_container(...)
    self.add_item(container)          <- the card
    self.add_item(ActionRow(...))     <- and the buttons, beside it

That is valid, it compiles, nothing warns -- and it renders below the
card, which is exactly the pre-V2 look the whole conversion was meant to
remove. The buttons now go into the container, behind a separator.

Checked across all 67 V2 classes: this was the only one.

Custom emoji
------------
The twelve J2C buttons carried the platform's hourglass, padlock, globe
and so on. All twelve now use the app's own -- ztimer, lock, zmsg,
zcross, universitybot_mention, zban, zCloud, unlock, starr, shuffle,
delete, Denied -- each verified to exist in tests/data/app_emojis.json
rather than assumed.

Eight more elsewhere: the sticky message setup, the autorole notice, the
help menu and the nuke alert. Zero buttons in the bot carry a platform
emoji now.

Nothing else changed about the panel: same labels, same styles, same
custom_ids, so the persistent view keeps working across restarts.

Verified: 52 test files pass, 146 cogs load, and all 14 mutations fail
the suite when reintroduced -- including the buttons going back outside
the container, a button losing its emoji, and a custom_id being dropped.

Three new checks guard this from here: components must be added to a
Container and never to the view, the J2C panel is asserted in full, and
no button anywhere may carry a platform emoji.

been seen rendered.

commits.subject: feat(bot): move the last buttons inside the card
commits.body:
After the embed conversion, plain discord.ui.Views were the only thing
left with the old look: their buttons hang *below* the message instead
of sitting in the container with the text. 28 sends across 12 files now
go through a new utils.panels.from_view(), and the calculator was
rebuilt as a LayoutView outright.

Counting it honestly
--------------------
The first scan said 401. That number was wrong four times over, and each
correction is worth writing down:

  * 189 of them were a variable called `view` and 100 called `embed` --
    the scan could not see what they were assigned. Following the
    assignment brought it to 102.
  * 41 of those were `_create_modern_embed`, a factory returning
    CV2EmbedAdapter -> CV2 -> LayoutView. Already V2. Following function
    returns brought it to 36.
  * More were `cog.build_panel` and `store.build_view`, methods on other
    modules that also return Panels.

83 sends across 19 classes were real. 28 could be rewritten
mechanically; the rest are classes that send themselves.

Two traps, both hit
-------------------
from_view() *moves* the components out of the view it is given, the same
way from_embed() does -- a component belongs to one view at a time. That
is correct for a view sent once and wrong for one that is edited later
with `view=self`: the second send arrives empty.

The calculator does exactly that on every keypress. Wrapping it left it
with no keys after the first press. Reverted, then rebuilt properly.

Rebuilding it was not a one-liner either: a LayoutView ignores @button
decorators -- checked, the class comes out with zero children -- and has
no `row=`, because rows are objects in V2. The 16 keys moved into five
ActionRow subclasses, the display moved into the panel, and the view
redraws itself rather than handing its children away.

Reverted on purpose
-------------------
utils/paginator.py, used in 50 places, returns embeds from its page
source. Converting it needs the whole class turned into a LayoutView and
its five decorator-based buttons rewritten. A half-finished attempt got
as far as stripping the embed out without a replacement -- and the test
suite stayed green, because nothing exercises the paginator's rendering.
It is back as it was; a silently blank paginator in 50 places is not a
trade worth making without a test that would have caught it.

Verified: 52 test files pass, 146 cogs load, and all 9 mutations fail
the suite when reintroduced -- including both traps above. Two mutation
patterns were wrong first: one matched a placeholder, and one matched
from_embed's timeout line rather than from_view's, since three functions
share it.

Not tested against real Discord: no token here.

commits.subject: feat(bot): convert every remaining embed to Components V2, losing no text
commits.body:
337 sends across 68 files. Nothing in the bot sends `embed=` any more --
verified by walking the AST, not by grepping.

Making it lossless first
------------------------
The existing from_embed() kept the title, description, fields and
footer, and silently dropped the author (102 uses), the thumbnail (81),
the embed url and the timestamp. Converting 342 embeds through it would
have deleted a lot of text quietly, so it was rewritten before anything
was converted:

  * author  -> a subtle line above the heading, keeping its link
  * embed url -> the heading becomes a markdown link
  * thumbnail -> a Section accessory, which is the V2 equivalent of the
    top-right image; if there is no text to attach it to it becomes a
    gallery rather than vanishing
  * timestamp -> a Discord <t:...> tag on the footer line, where the
    embed put it
  * inline fields stay in one block instead of becoming a stack of tiny
    sections, because V2 has no columns

Also added from_embeds(), because Battleship sends three embeds in one
message and V2 has no equivalent -- they merge into one container in the
original order.

Two real bugs found while doing it
----------------------------------
from_embed(None) raised AttributeError. A greeting can be plain text, so
two callers pass an optional embed straight through; wrapping that
turned a working path into a 500. It returns None now, so `view=None`
still means what it meant.

The first version of the rewrite script used ast.unparse() to re-render
each file. That destroyed every comment in it -- 21 in the first test
file, including the licence header. The script now edits the byte range
of each call instead, and refuses to write a file that came out with
fewer comment markers than it went in with.

Verified
--------
  * tests/test_embed_lossless.py builds embeds in all 256 combinations
    of the optional parts and asserts every string survives -- plus
    markdown, maximum-length content, line breaks and empty embeds.
  * repro/verify_no_text_lost.py goes further: it reads all 421 embeds
    the bot actually constructs, rebuilds each one, and checks every
    literal string comes out. Zero lost.
  * All 14 mutations of the converter fail the suite when reintroduced.
  * 51 test files pass, 146 cogs load, 540 prefix and 73 app commands.

Two test stubs needed updating, and both were the test's fault rather
than the code's: the error handler's fake ctx only recorded `embed=`, so
every check reported that the user was told nothing, and the welcome
stub dropped `view=` on the floor.

Not tested against real Discord: no token here. Nothing in this change
has been seen rendered in a client.

docs(lavalink): add a deployable Lavalink service and setup guide
commits.body:
The public nodes the bot falls back to are shared and rate limited --
measured at roughly four searches before a 429. Fine for trying music
out, not for a bot on 23 servers. This adds everything needed to run a
private one.

  lavalink/Dockerfile      the official image, pinned to the 4 series
  lavalink/application.yml the config, password read from the env
  lavalink/README.md       Railway setup, public nodes, own server

Deployed as a second Railway service in the same project, so the bot
reaches it over private networking -- no public endpoint, no egress.

Config notes worth keeping:

  * The built-in YouTube source is off. It has been broken since 2024;
    the youtube-source plugin replaces it, and running both makes them
    compete for the same requests.
  * The password has no default. Spring aborts start-up when the
    variable is missing, which is what should happen -- a Lavalink with
    no password is an open relay.
  * COPY --chown, because the image runs as the unprivileged `lavalink`
    user. A root-owned config it cannot read makes it fall back to
    defaults: no password, no plugins, and a failure that looks like
    "everything started fine but nothing plays".
  * The README calls out restartPolicyMaxRetries = 5 from the shared
    railway.toml. Five failed starts and Railway leaves the service
    down for good, even after the missing variable is added -- that
    needs a manual redeploy and is not obvious.

Verified: the image tag exists and its WorkingDir really is
/opt/Lavalink (read out of the image config rather than assumed), both
plugin jars resolve at the pinned versions (HTTP 200 from
maven.lavalink.dev), the YAML parses, and 4.2.2 is current.

Not verified, and the README says so plainly: whether Lavalink actually
starts with this config. There is no Docker and no Java 17 in this
environment, so it could not be run.

commits.subject: fix(music): both Lavalink hosts were dead, so /play could never work
commits.body:
The guard was right, the server was gone. Every /play answered "the
music server is not reachable" because it genuinely was -- both hosts
the bot could reach are down:

    lava-v4.ajieblogs.eu.org    404  the vhost no longer exists
    lavalink.jirayu.net:13592   500  "Proxy error: dial tcp
                                     38.49.216.39:2334: connection
                                     refused"

The second one is only a proxy, and the machine behind it refuses
connections. The 429 wavelink logged on the websocket for hours was that
same outage on a different route -- not throttling, an outage.

Replaced with two hosts that were checked by hand: /v4/info returns 200,
/v4/loadtracks returns real tracks, and a real wavelink node reaches
CONNECTED and searches successfully from this machine
(repro/lavalink_live.py does the whole thing end to end).

Now a list rather than a single host. LAVALINK_HOST still wins when set,
and each candidate gets ten seconds before moving on, so one dead host
cannot block the rest the way the previous single-host version did.

Both public hosts are rate limited -- measured at roughly four searches
before a 429 on the first, fewer on the second. That surfaced as "No
results found.", which sends people looking for a better search term
when the answer is "wait a few seconds". A 429 now raises
Music.RateLimited and says so.

These are free shared nodes and a stopgap, not a fix. Set LAVALINK_HOST
and LAVALINK_PASSWORD to a Lavalink of your own for anything serious.

Verified: 50 test files pass, 146 cogs load, all 19 mutations fail the
suite when reintroduced, and the live check connects and searches
successfully. One check needed fixing first -- it looked for
`raise Music.RateLimited()` as text, so changing its guard to
`if False:` left the line in place and passed.

tested against the real servers.

commits.subject: fix(bot): my own retry loop was dead code, and the guild log used a deleted channel
commits.body:
Two things the clean log made visible.

The retry loop never looped
---------------------------
The previous commit added this, and it was wrong:

    while not self.client.is_closed():
        await wavelink.Pool.connect(...)
        ...
        print("... Retrying in 30 seconds...")
        await asyncio.sleep(30)

Pool.connect() awaits node._connect(), and the websocket underneath has
its own unbounded reconnect loop. On a host that refuses the handshake
that await never returns -- so the while loop was parked in its first
iteration for good.

The tell was in the log: "Retrying in 30 seconds..." appeared exactly
once, three minutes after start-up, and never again. A loop that claims
a 30-second period and fires once is not looping.

It is now one attempt, started as a background task, with a bounded
20-second wait to see whether the node comes up. wavelink keeps
retrying by itself either way, so music still recovers when the host
does -- the difference is that our own message no longer promises
something it cannot do. The task is held on the cog because asyncio
only keeps a weak reference and would let it be collected mid-flight.

Worked out in repro/lavalink_loop.py against the installed wavelink,
not guessed from the docs.

The guild join/leave log
------------------------
    [00:38:06] -> Channel with ID 1396794297386532978 not found.

A hard-coded channel that no longer exists, logged at ERROR on every
join and every leave, with the message silently dropped -- while
`guild_log_channel` sat in the dashboard being ignored.
university_bot.py already reads that setting for the same event, so the
cog was the odd one out. It now reads it too, and an unconfigured
channel is a debug line rather than an error, because not wanting a
join log is a normal setup.

Verified: 50 test files pass, 146 cogs load, and all 14 mutations fail
the suite when reintroduced. One check needed fixing first -- it only
looked for `music_ready()` anywhere in the file, so replacing the poll
with `if True:` passed. It now requires the success line to sit inside
that check.

Not tested against real Discord or a working Lavalink node; neither is
reachable from here.

commits.subject: fix(bot): stop the Lavalink retry spam flooding the log
commits.body:
The crash is gone, but the log is now mostly one thing. From the latest
Railway output, repeating for as long as the bot runs:

    An unexpected error occurred while connecting Node(...) to Lavalink:
    "429, message='Invalid response status', ..."
    If this error persists or wavelink is unable to reconnect, ...
    Node(...) retrying websocket connection in "17.7" seconds.

Three lines per attempt, and wavelink retries forever -- the public host
answers 429 for hours, so this is the steady state, not a blip. In one
2.5-minute log it was 33 lines of the same message.

Two things made it that loud, and neither is a wavelink bug:

  * Three cogs call `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)`.
    basicConfig configures the *root* logger, so one cog switches on
    INFO for every library in the process -- which is the only reason
    wavelink's "retrying ..." line (a logger.info) appears at all.

  * Nothing narrowed wavelink's own level, so the 429 warning printed in
    full, footer and all, on every attempt.

utils/bootstrap.py now raises wavelink and httpx to ERROR. It runs at
import, before any cog, and a named logger's level is not touched by a
later basicConfig -- verified rather than assumed, since the cogs import
after it. music.py re-applies it when connecting, so a stray basicConfig
during start-up cannot resurrect the spam.

httpx is in there for the same reason: it narrates the dashboard calling
itself -- "HTTP Request: GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/..." -- immediately
next to our own request log line saying the same thing.

ERROR and not CRITICAL on purpose. A genuine failure still reaches the
log; only the routine retry chatter goes, and the one-line status
message added in the previous commit says whether music actually works.

Verified: the noise is measured before and after in
repro/lavalink_noise.py (30 lines per 10 attempts, down to 0), 50 test
files pass, 146 cogs still load, and all 11 mutations fail the suite
when reintroduced. One check passed against a tree with the start-up
call deleted -- the test was calling quieten_libraries() itself, so it
could not see that nothing else did.

Not tested against real Discord or a working Lavalink node; neither is
reachable from here.

commits.subject: fix(music): stop crashing when Lavalink is unreachable
commits.body:
From the Railway log:

    [ERROR] Unhandled error in 'play' (guild ..., user ...):
    InvalidNodeException: No nodes are currently assigned to the
    wavelink.Pool in a CONNECTED state.

The public Lavalink host was answering 429, so no node ever reached
CONNECTED. Every music command then died as an unhandled traceback and
the user in the channel got nothing back at all -- no reply, no error,
just silence.

A try/except around the command body would not have helped: wavelink
resolves the node inside Player.__init__, so
`channel.connect(cls=wavelink.Player)` raises before any of the cog's
code runs. It has to be checked before connecting. Music.music_ready()
does that, and require_music() turns it into a plain sentence in the
channel instead of a traceback in the log.

All four places that build a player are guarded now: play_source, join,
the track picker in SearchResultView, and the search command -- that
last one up front, rather than after the user has picked a platform and
a track from a menu that was never going to work. Moving an existing
player between channels still works without a node, since that does not
construct one.

Also fixed, and visible in the same log: the startup line claimed
success too early.

    Lavalink node connected: http://lavalink.jirayu.net:13592
    ... one second later ...
    An unexpected error occurred while connecting Node(...): 429

Pool.connect() returns as soon as the handshake is handed off, while the
websocket is still coming up, so "connected" was printed for a node that
then failed. It now waits for the node to actually reach CONNECTED
before saying so, and says plainly when it does not, so the log shows
whether music is available.

Verified: the crash is reproduced and then shown handled by
repro/music_no_node.py, 50 test files pass, 146 cogs still load, and all
7 mutations fail the suite when reintroduced.

Not tested against real Discord, and not against a working Lavalink
node: neither is reachable from here. What is tested is the path the log
actually hit -- no node at all.

commits.subject: test(dashboard): stop pinning the smoothing to an exact 120ms
commits.body:
The sidebar's time constant was tuned by hand to 10ms, and the check
failed against it -- a perfectly good setting. What matters is that both
lists ask for one and that it is usable; the hook divides by it, so zero
is the only value that actually breaks. The mutations now flip it to
zero instead of nudging it to a neighbouring number, and the three
patterns that had gone stale since the shift moved to 37px are matched
against the current values again.

commits.subject: feat(bot): convert embed+button messages to Components V2, use the custom emojis
commits.body:
Components V2
-------------
41 call sites that sent a classic embed together with a View now send a
V2 panel instead, so the buttons sit inside the card rather than under
it. They go through a new utils.panels.from_embed, which rebuilds the
embed as a Panel and carries the existing view's components across.

The components are moved, not copied. A component belongs to one view at
a time, and leaving it on the old view means discord.py keeps routing
its callback through a view that is never sent.

Scope, after counting properly three times: 453 embeds in total, 185
"with a view" -- but 81 of those are view=None, which is how a message
*removes* its buttons, and another 61 are embed=None on cogs already
migrated. 83 were real candidates; 41 have a plain `embed=<name>,
view=<name>` shape a script can rewrite safely. The rest build the embed
or the view inline, or pass file=/attachments= as well, and are left for
a human rather than rewritten by text.

Found while building it: _rows() chunked components five to a row by
count alone, so a select sharing a row with buttons raised "maximum
number of children exceeded" -- a select takes a whole row. It now
breaks the run.

Custom emojis
-------------
The app owns 142 emojis and the central tables were still handing back
the platform's white-on-grey marks. ACTION_EMOJIS, BUTTON_EMOJIS,
MINECRAFT_EMOJIS and the V2 status markers are custom now; 🎯 and ✏️
stay because the app has no counterpart, and a wrong custom icon is
worse than a right platform one.

CHECK/OK pointed at the platform ✅ while FAIL/NOT_OK next to them were
custom, so a success and a failure from the same command did not look
like they came from the same bot.

100 buttons that had no emoji got one, chosen from their label through a
new LABEL_EMOJIS table -- one place, so "Cancel" cannot end up with
three different icons. 27 were left bare on purpose: calculator keys,
format names like PNG, and labels built at runtime. Longest key wins, so
"Stop Freezing" does not pick up the plain stop icon.

Real bug fixed: PREVIOUS was <:next:>, the same right-pointing arrow as
NEXT_ALT1, so every "previous page" button in the paginator and the help
menu showed an arrow pointing forwards. Corrected to <:zback:>, which is
the app's only left-pointing arrow -- confirmed by looking at the
rendered images, not the names.

Verified: 146 cogs still load with 540 prefix and 73 app commands, 49
test files pass, and all 14 mutations fail the suite when reintroduced.
Four checks needed fixing first: two mutation patterns matched several
identical call sites, one fixture never exercised the rule it claimed to
test, and the embed+V2 check could not see from_embed() because it is a
function rather than a class -- an embed sent alongside it slipped
straight through.

Not tested against real Discord: no token here, and nothing in this
change was seen rendered in a client.
