Update layout.tsx
fix(dashboard): round the glow corner, widen the sidebar travel to 37px
commits.body:
The glow corner
---------------
The halo was square in the corners of a rounded card, which is what the
screenshot showed. The ring is an inset box-shadow, and an inset shadow
is painted on the padding box -- whose radius CSS derives by subtracting
the border width. The halo layer carries a 40px transparent border to
push the ring back onto the card's edge, so inheriting the card's 24px
gave 24 - 40, clamped to 0.

Adding the padding back cancels the subtraction. Because the radius now
has to be known rather than inherited, it comes from --card-radius,
defaulting to rounded-3xl (113 of the 121 cards); the 8 cards on other
radii carry .glow-r-2xl or .glow-r-20. The clipped variant has no border
to compensate for, so it uses the plain value.

Worked out in repro/glow_radius.py rather than guessed.

The sidebar travel
------------------
Now LineSidebar's own maxShift of 37px, up from 14. The nav had 16px of
room, and a scroll container clips at its padding box, so the padding
went with it: pl-4 pr-10. 40px clears the full travel with 3px spare and
is the most that fits -- at 44px "Zurueck zur Serverliste" starts to
wrap, which repro/prox_shift_budget.py now checks alongside the budget.

Sub-links go 10px -> 26px. The global search dropdown stays at 10px on a
new .prox-row-tight: it is not in the nav and has no spare padding of
its own to slide into, so it would have been clipped by its own edge.

Verified: 48 test files green, and all 31 mutations fail the suite when
reintroduced -- including the radius going back to inherit, the padding
shrinking back, and the dropdown inheriting the sidebar's travel. The
budget check no longer hard-codes the padding; the old copy went stale
the moment the nav changed and failed against correct CSS.

Not tested in a real browser: there is none in this environment.

commits.subject: feat(dashboard): BorderGlow rim on the cards, proximity on the tab rows
commits.body:
Two things from React Bits, both adapted rather than dropped in.

BorderGlow, on 121 cards
------------------------
The pointer's angle and its distance to the nearest edge go into two
custom properties; the rim and the halo are CSS reading those.

The brief's source had been pasted through Markdown, which corrupted six
places: a missing bracket in the glow-var loop, a broken template
literal on className, x * x * x collapsed to x  *x*  x by italics, and
three autolinked identifiers. That last kind is the dangerous one --
x  *x*  x still parses, it just computes a different curve. All
reconstructed rather than copied.

Structural change: one document listener that finds the card under the
pointer with closest(), instead of a handler and a rAF loop per card.
With 121 cards the original design means 121 of each for one cursor.
More importantly it makes applying the effect a class name, not a JSX
restructure -- the original wraps content in two extra divs, which would
have broken every grid and flex parent it was added to.

Dropped on purpose, both documented in the file: the inner mesh wash
(an element has two pseudos, the third layer is what forces the extra
markup -- and it does not render in Firefox, which has no
mask-composite: subtract), and the 'animated' intro sweep (it plays on
mount, and 121 rims sweeping at page load is not an intro; the brief's
own example switches it off).

Colours are the dashboard's blue and indigo, and the card keeps its own
background -- the original paints #120F17 over it, which would have
broken every bg-* override in the codebase. 16 cards clip their own
content and would have shown a halo cut off square; those get the
inside-only variant.

Which cards: the 121 big ones, chosen with the TypeScript parser rather
than a regex. The first pass judged nesting by indentation and skipped
51 real cards, because a sibling inside a .map() is indented deeper
without being nested. Tab strips, search inputs and single-row bars are
excluded -- a rim light on a text field reads as a focus ring firing on
hover.

Proximity on the tab rows
-------------------------
Your LineSidebar settings, unchanged where they transfer: radius 85,
smoothing 120, smooth falloff, no index and no marker.

Two could not transfer as-is. The hook measured y only, which is right
for a stacked list but lights an entire line at once on a row that
wraps, since those buttons share an offsetTop -- it now takes an axis
and the rows ask for real 2D distance. And maxShift 37 is a sideways
push on a vertical list, into empty space; these tabs sit shoulder to
shoulder with a 6px gap, so 37px sideways would bury two neighbours. The
travel is perpendicular here too -- vertical -- at 6px, which keeps the
button inside the strip, with the rest of the 37 in a slight scale.

Verified: 48 test files green, and all 23 mutations fail the suite when
reintroduced. Three checks passed against a mutated tree first: two
matched an identifier without checking what it was called with, and one
mutation only broke tsc rather than the behaviour, so it was replaced
with a regression that compiles.

Not tested in a real browser: there is none in this environment.

commits.subject: feat(dashboard): drop the tick marks, widen the shift, unify smoothing
commits.body:
The leading line is gone from both the sidebar and the search results.
A row that both slides and grows a line was two signals for one thing;
the movement alone says it.

Removing it also retires the marker CSS, the --prox-accent custom
property and the color-mix fallback that existed only to tint the line
-- color-mix is used nowhere else in this project.

Travel goes 8px -> 14px at the top level and 5px -> 10px for nested
rows, and smoothing is 120ms everywhere, matching the hook default that
the two call sites had drifted off (130 and 110).

14px is not a taste call. The nav is overflow-y: auto, so per CSS
Overflow 3 the other axis computes to auto too, and a scroll container
clips at its padding box. A 256px sidebar with 16px of nav padding
leaves exactly 16px of room; past that the row is clipped, or the nav
scrolls sideways under no-scrollbar where the scrollbar is hidden and
nobody would see it. 14px keeps 2px in hand. Worked out in
repro/prox_shift_budget.py and pinned by the suite, which now derives
the budget instead of hard-coding a number.

Verified: all 15 mutations fail the suite when reintroduced, including
the shift overflowing the padding edge and either call site drifting off
120ms. One check passed against a tree with the whole reduced-motion
block deleted -- splitting on the query name leaves a chunk running to
the end of the file, which matched the .prox-row rules below it. It now
cuts each block to its own body first.

Not tested in a real browser: there is none in this environment.

commits.subject: fix(dashboard): drop the row numbers and stop clipping the marker
commits.body:
The 01/02/03 gutter from LineSidebar is gone. It was the loudest thing
in a sidebar that is read by label, and nobody navigates by ordinal.

While removing it, a real bug in the marker turned up. It was placed at
left: -22px, outside a row that sits 16px inside a nav with
overflow-y-auto. Per CSS Overflow 3 a scroll container clips the other
axis too, so 6 of those 22px -- 27% of the line -- were cut off on every
row. It is now an in-flow flex child of fixed width with the line scaled
inside it, so nothing can clip it and the label does not move as the
effect changes.

Two more gaps closed:

  * Sub-links took no part at all. Inside a guild the sidebar is mostly
    sub-links, so the effect was invisible on most pages. One running
    index now covers both levels; nested rows get a shorter shift.
  * The search dropdown uses the same effect, with the keyboard cursor
    feeding activeIndex so arrowing down and hovering produce one
    highlight instead of two that can disagree.

useProximity now takes the container by ref instead of reading the first
row's offsetParent, which guessed wrong as soon as a wrapper appeared.

reduced-motion freezes the line at its resting length; transform: none
would have collapsed the scaleX and shown every marker at full width.

Verified: the clipping is reproduced by repro/prox_clip.py, and all
eight mutations -- numbers back, marker outside, reduced-motion at full
width, sub-links stripped, dropdown stripped, cursor unhooked, stale
rows kept, offsetParent guessing -- fail the suite when reintroduced.
Two of the new checks passed against a mutated tree at first: one
matched a marker rule outside the media query, the other matched the
word scaleX in a comment. Both now cut to the rule body and strip
comments first.

Not tested in a real browser: there is none in this environment.

commits.subject: feat(dashboard): LineSidebar proximity effect on the sidebar
commits.body:
Adapted from React Bits' LineSidebar rather than dropped in whole.

That component takes `items: string[]` and an `onItemClick`, and
renders `<li onClick>`. Our navigation is `<Link href>`. Using it as-is
would have replaced real links with click handlers and lost right-click
"open in new tab", middle-click, the URL preview in the corner and
Next.js prefetching — and it has no notion of the icons or the six
groups the guild sidebar is built from. The visual idea is worth
having; that trade is not.

So the mechanism is kept as a hook and the markup left alone. Each row
gets --effect between 0 and 1, eased toward its target by one shared
rAF loop with frame-rate independent smoothing, exactly as in the
original. Colour, shift and marker length all read that same value, so
they move as one thing instead of three CSS transitions drifting apart.
Marker lines and zero-padded indices are carried over.

Applied to the flat top-level rows only — Dashboard, Server, Premium,
Admin Panel. Inside a guild the sidebar is six groups of sub-links, and
lighting those by cursor distance fights the group headings.

Deliberately *not* on the admin tab row: the effect measures vertical
distance, and every button in a horizontal row shares an offsetTop, so
all twenty would light at once. That is a switch, not a proximity
effect. I wired it there first and took it back out; a test now keeps
it out.

Two things added on top of the original: touch drags are ignored,
because a drag is a scroll and reacting to it lights up whatever the
finger passes over; and the marker has a plain rgba before the
color-mix, since color-mix is used nowhere else in this project and an
unsupported declaration would leave it invisible.

The hook sits above the layout's early return — React runs every hook
on every render, and the loading branch returns before the sidebar is
built.

commits.subject: feat(dashboard): glass surfaces and live figures in the admin panel
commits.body:
Everything in the screenshot, rebuilt.

**Glass.** The header, the four stat cards and the tab bar were flat
navy boxes with hard 1px borders. Real glass needs three things at once
and none were there: a blur behind it, an edge brighter at the top than
the bottom, and an inner highlight. .admin-glass has all three, plus a
rim light drawn with a masked gradient rather than a border, so it fades
out towards the bottom the way an edge actually catches light. The
header sits over a slow colour wash that drifts behind the glass.

Two things that would otherwise break silently: the rim overlay is
pointer-events: none, or it would swallow every click on the card
underneath, and there is an @supports fallback because Firefox and
older Safari have no backdrop-filter and would render the near
transparent background as almost nothing.

**The LIVE badges are gone.** All four cards claimed "LIVE" while the
data refreshes every 30 seconds. That was a small lie, and four
identical badges said nothing anyway. They now show the real age —
"gerade eben", "vor 12 s" — and turn amber once the figure is older
than the refresh interval allows, which is exactly the case a green
badge was hiding. The timestamp is only set on success: stamping it in
`finally` would make a failed refresh look fresh while the old numbers
sit on screen.

**Figures animate to their new value** on every refresh, counting from
the previous one rather than snapping back to zero. They are strings
with units — "16.51ms", "0.94 MB" — so CountUp could not be used; the
number is split from its suffix, and anything with no number in it is
printed untouched instead of becoming NaN.

The interval for the age lives inside the badge, not the page: ticking
a clock in the parent re-renders twenty tab buttons and a table once a
second.

Two of my own test mistakes surfaced here. "backdrop-filter" matched
inside "-webkit-backdrop-filter", so the check passed with the
unprefixed property deleted — every non-Safari browser would have shown
a flat box. And the no-pulse check read everything from ".admin-link"
to the end of the file, which swept in the new header animation.
